name: Question 5
worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 2{\alpha }_{1}t \\ {\alpha }_{1}t & 3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues of $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=4t,
$$

both of multiplicity one. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}r(t)={e}^{t} \\ r(4t)={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t} \\ 4t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

- Subtracting the first equation from the second one, we get

$$
3t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}).
$$

- Multiplying the first equation by $4$ and subtracting the second one, we get

$$
3{\alpha }_{0}=4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{0}=\frac{1}{3}(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}).
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t & =(\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}))t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}), \\ 3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =3(\frac{1}{3t}({e}^{4t}-{e}^{t}))t+\frac{1}{3}(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((3{e}^{4t}-3{e}^{t})+(4{e}^{t}-{e}^{4t})) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2{e}^{4t}+{e}^{t}),\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t}+2{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{4t}-2{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{4t}-{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{4t}+{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$
